newsitem.title: UK: Intl bond issuance tops $400 bln in first half.
newsitem.headline: Intl bond issuance tops $400 bln in first half.

text.p: International bond issuance just topped $400 billion in the first half of the year for a 13.4 percent rise on the same period in 1996, itself the prior busiest January-June period, according to Capital DATA Bondware.

The dollar extended its dominance of the market, taking a 47.9 percent share with 839 deals worth $192 billion. In the first six months of 1996 it had a 39.8 percent ($141 billion) share. The dollar accounted for 41 percent of the market overall in all 1996.
The mark was the second most active currency in volume terms with 225 deals worth $50 billion, a 12.6 percent share after 17.7 percent ($63 billion) in the first half last year.
Sterling was third with 10.3 percent ($41 billion, 166 deals) after 7.2 percent ($25 billion) in 1996.
Historically low absolute levels of interest rates around the world have enticed borrowers into the market.
The $401 billion raised so far this year compares with the total $440 billion raised in all 1995, itself then a record year.
